# Claim vs counter-claim ledger

Two sections:
1. **Contradictions** - two credible primary sources disagree, unresolved.
2. **X-grade claims** - repeated in reviews but not traceable to primary data.
   Per the confidence scale these are high-value findings, not filler.

## 1. Contradictions

| id | Claim | Counter-claim | Refs | Load-bearing for | Status |
|----|-------|---------------|------|------------------|--------|
| c001 | Yengo 2022 (Nature, peer-reviewed): the 7,209 height-associated genomic segments have a **mean** size of ~90 kb | The bioRxiv preprint of the *same analysis* states a **median** of ~90 kb | `yengo2022` (10.1038/s41586-022-05275-y) vs preprint 10.1101/2022.01.07.475305 | `height_gwas` segment-size quantitative row; any downstream estimate of per-segment gene density | **Unresolved.** For a right-skewed segment-size distribution mean and median cannot both be ~90 kb, so one wording is loose. Published value used, discrepancy flagged on the node. Needs Supplementary Table retrieval to settle — queued P2 in access_queue.md. Neither number is load-bearing for a mechanistic claim, so impact is low. |
| C-L4-03 | **Glucocorticoids are pro-chondrogenic and RAISE SOX9.** Dexamethasone enhanced Sox9 mRNA and protein in newborn mouse rib chondrocytes within 24 h, dose-dependently from a threshold of 0.1 nM to a maximum at 10 nM, with parallel Col2a1 induction and no change in Sox9 mRNA half-life (~45 min) (`sekiya2001`). This is why 100 nM dexamethasone is a standard component of chondrogenic differentiation medium. | **Glucocorticoids SUPPRESS SOX9.** At 100 uM, glucocorticoid suppressed SOX9, COL2 and aggrecan protein and mRNA time- and dose-dependently in human knee articular chondrocytes through p38 inactivation, with the transcriptional effect appearing BEFORE any apoptotic effect (`song2012`) | `sekiya2001` (PMID 11375127) vs `song2012` (PMID 21898067) | `sox9_tf`, `glucocorticoid_cortisol`, `glucocorticoid_receptor`; edge e00066; any mechanistic account of glucocorticoid growth arrest that runs through loss of chondrogenic identity | **Unresolved.** The two studies differ by a 10,000-fold concentration range, by species (mouse vs human) and by cartilage type (rib growth cartilage vs knee articular). Recorded in the atlas as `sign: biphasic` rather than resolved. If the low-dose limb is the physiological one, glucocorticoid growth arrest is NOT a SOX9 lesion and must run through local GH/IGF-1 resistance (`jux1998`), IHH suppression (`zaman2019`) and PI3K-AKT-dependent apoptosis (`chrysis2005`) instead. Opened as gap `g_l4l3_006`. |
| C-L4-04 | **TRalpha1 is the thyroid hormone receptor that carries T3 action in cartilage.** The in vivo skeletal phenotype of thyroid hormone receptor mutants is dominated by TRalpha: THRA mutations produce the skeletal dysplasia of resistance to thyroid hormone alpha, and TRalpha is the receptor whose deletion reproduces the growth plate phenotype | **All T3 responses in primary chondrocytes require TRbeta.** T3 decreased proliferation and accelerated differentiation in wild-type and TRalpha-deficient mouse rib chondrocytes, but every T3 response was ABROGATED in TRbeta-deficient chondrocytes; T3 also raised TRbeta1 expression selectively (`rabier2006`). Independently, THRbeta1 binds a thyroid hormone response element in the distal Ihh promoter and the TRbeta-selective agonist GC1 raises epiphyseal Ihh ~100-fold (`xing2016`) | `rabier2006` (PMID 17065405), `xing2016` (PMID 27026086), `aghajanian2017` (PMID 28874841) vs the THRA human and mouse genetics summarised on `thra_receptor` | `thra_receptor`, `thrb_receptor`, `ihh_protein`; edges e00046, e00047, e00057, e00058; the choice of receptor isoform for any thyromimetic intended to act on cartilage | **Unresolved.** Possible reconciliations: cell-autonomous versus systemic action (TRbeta may carry the chondrocyte-intrinsic response while the in vivo phenotype is dominated by TRalpha-mediated systemic effects); site (rib and epiphysis versus long-bone physis); or developmental window (SOC formation versus postnatal physeal growth). `aghajanian2017` adds a third possibility that the two isoforms are genuinely antagonistic, TRalpha1 raising SHH and TRbeta1 raising IHH while suppressing SHH. No study has deleted each receptor specifically in growth plate chondrocytes and scored zonal architecture. |
| C-L2-01 | **The skeletal stem cell is a definable cell with a marker panel.** Five schemes each claim the apex position: mSSC (CD45−Ter119−Tie2−AlphaV+Thy−6C3−CD105−CD200+), PTHrP+/FoxA2+ resting chondrocytes, Grem1+ metaphyseal OCR cells, LepR+ perisinusoidal stroma, CTSK-lineage periosteal stem cells | The schemes are **mutually incompatible on anatomy, markers, adipogenic potential and developmental window.** PTHrP+ resting cells are Grem1-negative; LepR+ cells never contribute to developing cartilage and dominate osteoblast production only after adolescence; the PSC carries the *same* CD200+CD105−Thy−6C3− immunophenotype as the mSSC but in a different compartment, so the mSSC panel does not specify anatomical identity | `chan2015`, `worthley2015`, `zhou2014`, `debnath2018`, `mizuhashi2018`, `shu2021` | Any therapeutic inference from L2; the choice of mouse model that reports on human growth; L7 fusion models that assume a single depletable progenitor pool | **Unresolved.** No study applies all panels and all Cre drivers to one cohort at matched ages with one functional assay. Only cross-scheme quantification located is `mizuhashi2018` (PTHrP+ vs mSSC/pre-BCSP/BCSP tiers, and Grem1 exclusion). Opened as gap `g_l2stem_004`. |
| C-L2-02 | **The human skeletal stem cell is PDPN+CD146−CD73+CD164+ and does not make fat** (`chan2018`); CD146+ cells are inferior colony formers | **The human skeletal stem cell is the CD146+ subendothelial adventitial reticular cell**, which self-renews, transfers the hematopoietic microenvironment and *does* generate marrow adipocytes (`sacchetti2007`, `bianco2015`) | `chan2018` vs `sacchetti2007` / `bianco2015` | `human_skeletal_stem_cell`, `marrow_stromal_cell`; every translational claim built on prospectively sorted human skeletal progenitors | **Unresolved.** The two definitions are CD146-positive and CD146-negative respectively, and disagree on adipogenesis — the property Bianco uses to define bona fide skeletal stemness. Both rest on heterotopic transplantation of human cells into mice, so neither observes the cell in situ. |
| C-L2-03 | **The growth plate stem cell lives in the resting zone** — mouse PTHrP-creER and FoxA2-creER tracing, plus label-retention, all place it at the top of the plate | **The human SSC was localised to the second half of the pre-hypertrophic zone and the first half of the hypertrophic zone** (p-H2/H1) of a 17-week fetal femur, by scoring 76 mSSC/mBCSP orthologues and confirming by flow cytometry; the resting zone was not reported as an hSSC site | `mizuhashi2018`, `muruganandan2022`, `hallett2021` vs `chan2018` | `human_skeletal_stem_cell`, `resting_zone_niche`, `pthrp_positive_resting_chondrocyte`; whether mouse resting-zone biology describes humans at all | **Unresolved.** Either human and mouse growth plate stem cells occupy different zones — a major biological difference — or one localisation is an assay artefact. Never directly tested; opened as gap `g_l2stem_009`. |
| C-L2-04 | **Resting zone progenitors have a finite proliferative capacity that is monotonically spent, producing growth plate senescence** (`nilsson2004`, `schrier2006`) | **Chondroprogenitors are *depleted* during fetal/neonatal growth but then *acquire* self-renewal postnatally**, forming large stable monoclonal columns — capacity is gained, not only spent (`newton2019`) | `schrier2006`, `nilsson2004`, `gafni2001` vs `newton2019`, `mizuhashi2018` | `finite_proliferative_capacity_model`, `clonal_exhaustion`, `rz_depletion_causes_fusion`, and all of L7 | **Partly reconcilable, unresolved.** Species differ (rabbit/rat vs mouse) and so do levels (population kinetics vs clone counting); a plate could acquire self-renewal and still exhaust. But the two literatures have never been run in one system, and the finite-capacity model's own authors showed the in vitro Hayflick version is false (`nilsson2005`: rabbit RZ population doublings independent of donor age). Opened as gaps `g_l2stem_005` and `g_l2stem_008`. |
| C-L2-05 | **PTHrP (Pthlh) marks the growth plate stem cell** (`mizuhashi2018`, and the majority of the murine follow-up literature) | **The most stem-like population of the human pubertal resting zone is PTHLH-negative**; it expresses multiple SSC markers, sits in a WNT/TGF-β-low microenvironment, and maps to Prrx1+ mouse cells (`chu2026`). Separately, FoxA2+ cells are non-overlapping with PTHrP+ cells at labelling (0.017% double-positive = background) and outlive them in culture by ~6-fold (`muruganandan2022`) | `mizuhashi2018` vs `chu2026`, `muruganandan2022` | `pthrp_positive_resting_chondrocyte`, `prrx1_root_stem_cell`, `foxa2_resting_chondrocyte`; any attempt to use PTHrP as a human biomarker or drug target for growth | **Unresolved.** The field's flagship marker may not identify the analogous human cell. `chu2026` full text was not accessible (queued P1 in access_queue.md), so the strength of the PTHLH-negative claim rests on the abstract. |

| C-L3-01 | **FGFR3-STAT1 mediates the chondrocyte proliferation arrest that causes achondroplasia.** FGF phosphorylates STAT1, raises p21WAF1/CIP1, and Stat1-null metatarsals fail to arrest proliferation (`sahni1999`); the TD II K650E mutant constitutively activates STAT1 (`su1997`) | **Human thanatophoric dysplasia chondrocytes have no proliferation defect.** Primary fetal TD I chondrocytes showed a mitogenic response to FGF2 and FGF9 indistinguishable from controls; the lesion was ligand-independent STAT activation with nuclear STAT1 in hypertrophic cells and increased apoptosis (BAX up, BCL-2 down) (`legeaimallet1998`). Independently, deleting *Stat1* in achondroplasia-mutant mice restores proliferation but rescues neither the hypertrophic zone nor the dwarfism (`murakami2004`) | `sahni1999`, `su1997` vs `legeaimallet1998`, `murakami2004` | `fgfr3_stat1_branch`, `fgfr3_mapk_branch`, `mek1_erk_chondrocyte`; the choice of preclinical endpoint for every FGFR3-directed drug programme | **Unresolved.** The species split is the crux: the proliferation-arrest phenotype is rat/mouse, the human lesion is apoptosis-and-differentiation. No study measures proliferation index, phospho-ERK and phospho-STAT1 together in situ by zone in human dysplastic growth plate against matched controls. Opened as gap `g_l3core_008`. |
| C-L3-02 | **PDE5 is the dominant cGMP-hydrolysing phosphodiesterase of growth plate chondrocytes, but raising cGMP does not lengthen bone.** In newborn rat epiphyseal chondrocytes PDE5 was the major activity; tadalafil raised peak CNP-stimulated cGMP 37% and whole-tissue cGMP 52% (P<0.01), yet 3 weeks of treatment produced no change in long bone length, cortical or trabecular properties, or growth plate histology (`wang2018`) | **PDE3B is the functional cGMP PDE and inhibiting it does lengthen bone.** In mouse, cilostazol and milrinone raised chondrocyte cGMP, activated PKG-dependent K+ channels, promoted TRPM7-mediated Ca2+ entry, elongated cultured bones and enlarged juvenile animals; *Pde3b*-null mice have longer tibiae (`kawabe2025`, `miyazaki2022`) | `wang2018` vs `kawabe2025`, `miyazaki2022` | `pde_isoform_inventory`, `pde5a`, `pde3b`, `cgmp_second_messenger`; the entire premise that raising cGMP raises growth, on which CNP analogues, NPR3 decoys and PDE-inhibitor repurposing all rest | **Unresolved.** Cannot currently be attributed to species (rat vs mouse), isoform (PDE5 vs PDE3B), or compartment (bulk vs microdomain cGMP). Note the clinical stake: children with pulmonary arterial hypertension receive chronic PDE5 inhibitors and no growth plate follow-up has been reported. Opened as gap `g_l3core_007`. |
| C-L3-03 | **NPR2/GC-B is expressed in the prehypertrophic chondrocyte layer**, with CNP in the non-hypertrophic layers — the localisation used to argue for a short-range local CNP/GC-B system (`nakao2015`, citing the same group's earlier IHC) | **NPR2 transcript is present at similar levels in all three zones**; what is zone-restricted is the effector, PKG-I and PKG-II being expressed at much higher levels in hypertrophic cells, which the authors offer as the explanation for the spatial distribution of CNP effects (`agoston2007`, zonal microarray of microdissected mouse tibia) | `nakao2015` vs `agoston2007` | `npr2_receptor`, `pkg2_kinase`, `cnp_protein`, `pde_isoform_inventory`; whether the zonal partition of CNP action is set at the receptor or at the effector | **Unresolved, and consequential.** If the receptor is uniform and the effector is zoned, then CNP-analogue dosing acts on a tissue whose response is gated downstream of the drug target, and PKG/PDE distribution rather than receptor distribution sets where the drug works. The two studies used different modalities (IHC vs zonal microarray) and were never reconciled. |
| C-L3-04 | **SOX9 is required for chondrocyte hypertrophy.** Doxycycline-inducible Sox9 deletion in the mouse growth plate shows SOX9 is needed both to maintain columnar proliferation and to generate hypertrophy; SOX9 protein outlives its mRNA into upper hypertrophic cells, where it acts with MEF2C to directly activate *Col10a1* (`dy2012`) | **SOX9 must be switched off for chondrocytes to differentiate.** Activated mutant FGFR3 impairs endochondral bone growth specifically by *preventing SOX9 downregulation* in differentiating chondrocytes, i.e. persistent SOX9 is the achondroplasia lesion, not the growth-permitting state (`zhou2015`). Consistently, sustained Notch signalling suppresses *Sox9*, and that suppression is required for the onset of maturation (`kohn2015`) | `dy2012` vs `zhou2015`, `kohn2015` | `sox9_tf`, `pathway_convergence_node`, `runx2_tf`, `mef2c_tf`; and the direction of any therapeutic that raises or lowers SOX9 in achondroplasia | **Unresolved.** The two positions may be reconcilable as a biphasic requirement - SOX9 needed to license *Col10a1* at the prehypertrophic step but needing to fall for terminal maturation - but no experiment titrates SOX9 within a single differentiating population and measures hypertrophy as a continuous function of it. Opened as gap `g_l3rest_012`. |
| C-L1-01 | **Chondrocyte columns are the architecture that channels hypertrophic volume increase into longitudinal growth, and column formation is required for elongation.** A century of 2D histology plus the mutant literature (Itgb1, Cdh2, alpha-parvin) treats columnar order as the elongation-enabling structure | **Columns are rare precisely when elongation is fastest.** 3D multicolour clonal analysis of the E18.5 mouse growth plate found only 17.6% (distal femur, n=1044 doublets) and 19.4% (proximal tibia, n=805) of clonal doublets stacked at the 60-90 degree elevation angle that indicates a completed division-plane rotation; most embryonic clones are ellipsoidal clusters oriented **orthogonal** to the growth axis. Even at P40, within structures scored as columns, only 36-40% of divisions had completed rotation and under 10% were near-perfect | `rubin2024` vs `aszodi2003`, `romereim2014`, `greer2024`, `yuan2023` | `chondrocyte_column_formation`, `clonal_column`, `chondrocyte_cluster`, `appositional_growth`; the interpretation of every chondrodysplasia described as a "column disorganisation" phenotype | **Unresolved.** No experiment dissociates columnar order from hypertrophic cell volume: every published column mutant also perturbs cell shape, matrix or proliferation, so shortening cannot be attributed to loss of stacking alone. Opened as gap `g_l1arch_004`. |
| C-L1-02 | **Linear growth is saltatory**: infant length accrues in 0.5-2.5 cm bursts separated by 2-63 day intervals of true stasis, with 90-95% of days growth-free (`lampl1992`); canine proximal tibial growth measured with implanted tantalum markers is likewise reported to follow saltation and stasis (`mcbrien2011`) | **Linear growth is continuous.** Rabbit proximal tibial elongation measured directly with about 15-fold better precision than human anthropometry gave a single Gaussian distribution of daily velocities, not the bimodal distribution the saltation model predicts (`klein1994`); a further Science critique followed (`heinrichs1995`). A third position holds that short-term growth is a chaotic series of mini growth spurts with no true stasis (`hermanussen1998`) | `lampl1992`, `mcbrien2011` vs `klein1994`, `heinrichs1995`, `hermanussen1998`; methodological defence in `johnson1996` | `saltation_stasis_growth`, `growth_velocity_longitudinal`; the interpretation of every short-interval auxological endpoint, including the knemometry endpoints used in inhaled-corticosteroid safety trials | **Unresolved, and the two camps have never measured the same preparation.** The pro-saltation human evidence is surface anthropometry whose technical error exceeds the mean daily increment; the anti-saltation evidence is direct but in rabbit. One discontinuity is not in dispute: implanted microtransducers show at least 90% of lamb tibial elongation occurs during recumbency (`noonan2004`), so growth is load-gated on a diurnal cycle regardless of how the multi-day statistics are read. `heinrichs1995` has no indexed abstract anywhere and is queued P1 in access_queue.md. Opened as gaps `g_l1arch_005` and `g_l1arch_006`. |
| C-L1-03 | **Final hypertrophic chondrocyte volume is the principal determinant of elongation rate across species**, correlating with growth rate at r=0.98 in rat and r=0.83 in pig over a wide range of rates and volumes (`breur1991`) | **The relationship does not hold in birds.** Applied to four weight-bearing growth plates each in two-week-old mallard ducklings and leghorn chicks with direct fluorochrome measurement of elongation, the positive linear mammalian relationship between mean hypertrophic chondrocyte volume and bone elongation rate was not reproduced (`barreto1994`) | `breur1991`, `wilsman1996` vs `barreto1994` | `hypertrophic_volume_increase`, `hypertrophic_chondrocyte`, `elongation_budget`; whether a hypertrophy-volume readout is a valid preclinical surrogate for elongation at all | **Unresolved as a general rule; the regression slope already differs between rat and pig, so the relationship is not even a fixed mammalian constant.** No human measurement of final hypertrophic volume with unbiased stereology exists to place humans on (or off) the mammalian line. Opened as gap `g_l1arch_009`. |
| C-L1-07 | **Human terminal hypertrophic chondrocyte height is 33 ± 5 µm**, measured in the distal femur of 12 necropsy subjects aged birth to 14 y, five groups of ten cells per specimen, celloidin embedding with a measured 13 % linear processing shrinkage corrected for; the full series spans 29–38 µm with no age dependence (`kember1976`) | **It is 20.5 µm**, measured in the distal femur of one 10-year-old girl, 20 cells, decalcified paraffin with no shrinkage correction reported; the same study gives 26 µm in an 18-month-old's metatarsals (`thurston1985`) | `kember1976` vs `thurston1985` | `hypertrophic_chondrocyte`, `distal_femur_plate`, `cell_cycle_time_pz`; the `h_term_um` factor in `flow_model.py`, and through it **every** derivation of the human proliferative cell cycle time — the atlas's single largest source of model uncertainty | **Unresolved, and a 61 % disagreement on the same quantity, same bone, same species.** The lower value lies outside the entire range of the larger series, and reaching it from 33 µm requires **38 % linear shrinkage**. The methodological asymmetry runs one way on every axis — 12 subjects vs 1, ~50 cells vs 20, celloidin vs paraffin, shrinkage measured and corrected vs not reported — which favours the higher value without settling it, because neither study measured the other's specimens and no third human series exists. **Not averaged.** The flow-model span is stamped `CONTRADICTION`, not `MEASURED_SPREAD`. The decisive experiment is cheap and stated in `g_l1arch_009`: measure the transverse diameter and re-measure the axial height on archival human physeal sections with a stated, measured shrinkage correction. See `audit/corrections.md` CORR-008. |

| C-L7-01 | **Terminal growth plate chondrocytes are cleared by apoptosis**, the account carried into fusion by default from the rodent hypertrophic-chondrocyte literature | **The one human growth plate ever examined at the moment of fusion contained zero TUNEL-positive cells**, no detectable cleaved caspase-3 or Bax (only Bad among pro-apoptotic proteins), and no ultrastructural apoptosis or autophagy - instead showing hypoxia and necrosis (`emons2009`). Independently, estrogen-accelerated resting-zone cell loss in rabbit "did not appear to be due to apoptosis" (`nilsson2014`) | `emons2009`, `nilsson2014` vs the murine apoptosis literature | `apoptosis_at_fusion`, `hypoxia_necrosis_at_fusion`, `epiphyseal_fusion`; and the grading of every rodent apoptosis result transferred into L7 | **Unresolved, and unresolvable at present sample size.** The human refutation is n=1 fusing specimen, with no published positive control demonstrating the TUNEL assay would have detected apoptosis in that tissue block. No second human fusing plate has been reported in the 17 years since. Opened as gap `g_l7fuse_006`; the tissue-supply obstacle is `g_l7fuse_002`. |
| C-L7-02 | **"Rodents do not fuse their growth plates"** - the standard statement used to explain why fusion cannot be studied in mice (`emons2011`) | **Mice do form countable transphyseal bony bridges**, hundreds per tibial plate in wild types (495, SD 45; density 1.2, SD 0.5), rising ~12-fold in density in Socs2-/- animals, which the authors describe as *accelerated growth plate fusion* (`samvelyan2022`); yet the same plate is still calcified cartilage at 55 weeks, having LOST rather than gained type X collagen and MMP-13 (`yu2025`) | `emons2011` vs `samvelyan2022`, `yu2025` | `mouse_does_not_fuse`, `bony_bridge_formation`, `species_transfer_risk_fusion`, and the translation_risk grade on every murine node in the atlas | **Terminological, but consequential.** Both are true at their own level: mice bridge but never complete cartilage-to-bone replacement. The risk is that "accelerated fusion" in mouse papers is read as the human endpoint. This atlas resolves it by scoring bridge formation and epiphyseal fusion as separate nodes and by treating murine bridge counts as a surrogate whose relation to the human endpoint has never been validated. |
| C-L7-03 | **Better bone age assessment should improve prediction of remaining growth**, the premise of five decades of methodological work from Bayley-Pinneau through TW Mark II to BoneXpert | **A model that omits skeletal age entirely (Khamis-Roche) has errors only slightly larger than the RWT model that uses it** (`khamis1994`); and although automated reading cuts repeat-measurement SD to 0.17 y from a human interobserver spread of 0.74-0.96 y (`thodberg2009`, `king1994`), no study has demonstrated a corresponding narrowing of the adult height prediction interval | `khamis1994` vs `tanner1975`, `tanner1983`, `roche1975` | `remaining_growth_prediction`, `bone_age_measurement_error`, `automated_bone_age_ai`; the power calculation of every trial powered on predicted adult height | **Unresolved.** If most prediction error is irreducible biological variance rather than measurement error, then bone age precision is not the rate-limiting step in growth medicine and trials need larger n rather than better imaging. The variance decomposition has never been published. Opened as gap `g_l7fuse_007`. |
| c-L6-01 | Does dynamic loading spare growth, or only spare tissue? | `sergerie2011` (swine explants, matched strain) and `stokes2005` (rat, 12 vs 24 h/day) support "dynamic/intermittent loading is growth- and tissue-sparing", and `frost1979` predicts it theoretically | `valteau2011` applied sustained 0.2 MPa and sinusoidal 0.2 MPa +/-30% at 0.1 Hz to the same rat caudal vertebral level and found **identical 19% growth suppression** in both, with only the histomorphometry spared under dynamic loading | Not equivalent designs. `stokes2005` varied **duty cycle** (load off for 12 h/day); `valteau2011` varied **waveform** about a non-zero mean with the load never removed. Reviews routinely conflate the two under "dynamic". Current reading: mean stress integrated over time sets growth rate, waveform sets tissue damage. Unresolved - gap `g_l6mech_004` specifies the orthogonal 2x3 factorial that would settle it | `static_vs_dynamic_loading`, `wolff_law`, `strain_frequency_dependence` |
| c-L6-02 | Does gymnastics training reduce attained adult stature, or does gymnastics select short, late-maturing girls? | `theintz1993` (PHV 5.48 vs 8.0 cm/yr vs swimmers, falling height SDS, selective leg-length stunting, **no change in the chronological-age/bone-age ratio**) and the within-sport dose gradient in `daly2005` (peripubertal sitting-height velocity 2.3 vs 3.1 cm/yr by training volume) | `thomis2005` (spurts present, ~1 year late, matching short late-maturing girls with short parents) and the FIG Scientific Commission review `malina2013`, which finds epidemiological criteria for causality unmet and training volume inseparable from selection, energy availability and maturation | Both sides are right about different things. The attenuation **during** training is real and dose-related; the claim that it removes **adult** height is not established. Neither side has separated mechanical loading of the physis from energy deficit and hypothalamic suppression. Gap `g_l6mech_010` proposes the within-athlete segment contrast (heavily loaded distal radius vs lightly loaded lower limb, with energy availability measured) that would separate them | `gymnastics_stature_effect`, `sport_specific_loading_human` |

| c_l4endo_01 | Thyroid hormone action on growth plate chondrocytes is mediated by **TRbeta**: in primary neonatal rib chondrocytes from TRalpha- and TRbeta-deficient mice, T3 lowered proliferation and accelerated differentiation normally without TRalpha but ALL T3 responses were abolished without TRbeta | Thyroid hormone action on human stature is mediated by **TRalpha**: heterozygous dominant-negative THRA variants cause growth retardation, delayed bone age and disharmonious short stature, whereas dominant-negative THRB (RTHbeta) is common and typically NOT associated with short stature | `rabier2006` (PMID 17065405) vs `jorge2025` (PMID 38744258); localisation does not adjudicate - `robson2000` (PMID 11014246) finds TRalpha1, TRalpha2 AND TRbeta1 in rat reserve/proliferating zone and none in hypertrophic cells | `thra_receptor`, `thrb_receptor`, `thyroid_hormone_t3`; and the paediatric skeletal safety of TRbeta-selective thyromimetics (resmetirom class) | **Unresolved.** Possible reconciliations: rib versus long-bone chondrocytes are different skeletal elements; germline knockouts permit compensation a conditional deletion would not; or the isoform assignment genuinely differs between mouse and human. Opened as gap `g_l4endo_007` with a conditional-deletion plus human-chondrocyte discriminating experiment. |
| c_l4endo_02 | Glucocorticoid suppresses growth by acting **directly and potently inside the plate**: unilateral intra-growth-plate dexamethasone (80 ng/uL at 1 uL/h) cut ipsilateral rabbit proximal tibial growth by 77% versus the vehicle-infused contralateral plate (P<0.0001), and subsequent catch-up was likewise confined to the treated plate | **Endogenous glucocorticoid signalling in chondrocytes is dispensable**: tamoxifen-inducible chondrocyte-specific GR knockout mice had normal knee architecture, cartilage structure, growth plates, intervertebral discs, long bone length and bone microarchitecture at every age tested, with impairment only in metaphyseal fracture healing | `baron1992` (PMID 1415528) and `baron1994` (PMID 7925098) vs `tu2014` (PMID 25193158) | `glucocorticoid_cortisol`, `glucocorticoid_receptor`; whether a growth-sparing corticosteroid is achievable and what it would have to avoid | **Unresolved.** The two designs answer different questions (pharmacological excess versus loss of endogenous tone) but are routinely cited as if they answered the same one. The decisive experiment - unilateral local dexamethasone infusion IN a chondrocyte-specific GR knockout - has never been done. Opened as gap `g_l4endo_011`. |
| c_l4endo_03 | Seasonal variation in human height velocity peaks in **summer** and scales with photoperiod: in 2,277 GH-treated prepubertal children height velocity rose 0.146 cm/yr per daylight hour with no independent effect of calendar month, and in 9,409 Japanese infants length z-velocity peaked in summer with a winter-summer difference of 0.0026 z/day (~13% of mean velocity) | Seasonal variation peaks in **winter-spring** and is not isolated to height: in 760 Danish 8-11 year olds height velocity exceeded the 6.10 cm/yr mean in January-April, and - unlike the classical account of a spring height peak with an autumn weight peak - weight, BMI and fat-free mass index peaked coincidentally | `shulman2013` (PMID 23374591) and `narumi2020` (PMID 33102789) vs `dalskov2016` (PMID 26488554) | `seasonality_growth_velocity`, `growth_velocity_measurement_interval`; and the interpretation of any growth trial shorter than 12 months | **Unresolved.** Age (infants vs schoolchildren), latitude (Japan ~35 N, Denmark ~56 N), GH treatment status and measurement method all differ between the cohorts, and photoperiod, temperature and seasonal nutrition have never been separated in one design. Opened as gap `g_l4endo_008`. |
| c_l4endo_04 | Growth is driven by **circulating** IGF-1 (somatomedin hypothesis) - the axis's clinical biochemistry, human IGF1/IGFALS/STAT5B/GHR/PAPPA2 mutations and the LID+ALSKO threshold experiment all point to serum IGF-1 setting stature | Growth is driven by **locally produced** IGF-1 (dual effector) - liver-specific Igf1 deletion cut serum IGF-1 by 75% with no change in body weight, body length or femoral length in two independent mouse lines, and local GH action on the plate is abolished by somatomedin antiserum | `yakar1999` (PMID 10377413) and `sjgren1999` (PMID 10359843) vs `yakar2002` (PMID 12235108) and `domen2004` (PMID 14762184); local arm from `nilsson1986` (PMID 3523759), `schlechter1986` (PMID 3464007), `lui2019` (PMID 30765323) | `somatomedin_hypothesis`, `dual_effector_hypothesis`, `igf1_systemic`, `igf1_local_growth_plate`; and the choice between rhGH, rhIGF-1 and cartilage-targeted IGF-1 as therapy | **Partially resolved, but only in mouse.** A threshold model reconciles them: circulating IGF-1 is non-limiting until it falls below the LID+ALSKO level, at which point growth plate height, BMD and cortical thickness all drop and are restored by IGF-1.
