gap_contradictions.question: Are chondrocyte columns actually required for longitudinal elongation, given that they are rare in the embryonic growth plate at the time elongation is fastest?
gap_contradictions.why_it_matters: Column architecture is the canonical explanation for how hypertrophic volume increase is channelled into the longitudinal axis. If bones elongate fastest at a stage when fewer than one in five clonal doublets is correctly stacked, the causal role of columns — and the interpretation of every chondrodysplasia described as a 'column disorganisation' phenotype — needs revision.
gap_contradictions.what_is_known: Rubin et al. 2024 analysed 1044 distal-femur and 805 proximal-tibia clonal doublets in E18.5 mouse by 3D Confetti imaging and found only 17.6% and 19.4% respectively were stacked at elevation angles of 60-90 degrees; most clones were ellipsoidal clusters oriented orthogonal to the growth axis (rubin2024). Postnatally (P40) complete rotations rose to ~36-40% within columns, and perfect (80-90 degree) rotations were still under 10%. In parallel, the classical literature (aszodi2003, romereim2014, greer2024, yuan2023) treats column formation as necessary, and mutants that fail to form columns are short.
gap_contradictions.what_is_missing: A direct test of whether elongation rate depends on columnar order at fixed hypertrophic cell volume. Existing column mutants also perturb cell shape, matrix and proliferation, so shortening cannot be attributed to loss of stacking alone.
gap_contradictions.nearest_evidence_note: rubin2024 (mouse, 3D clonal); romereim2014 and aszodi2003 (mouse, rotation mechanism); reno2025 (metatarsals and pisiform grow from a single plate, showing plate architecture is not stereotyped).
gap_contradictions.discriminating_experiment: In an allelic series that graduates column disorder without changing chondrocyte volume (for example titrated chondrocyte-specific Itgb1 or Cdh2 alleles), measure by 3D imaging both the fraction of correctly stacked doublets and the final hypertrophic cell volume, and measure elongation by calcein double labelling. If elongation rate scales with hypertrophic volume and is insensitive to stacking fraction over a 20-60% range, columns are a lateral-confinement convenience rather than the elongation engine. If elongation falls with stacking fraction at matched cell volume, columns are causal.

gap_contradictions.question: Is longitudinal bone growth genuinely saltatory — alternating true-zero-velocity stasis with discrete elongation bursts — or continuous with measurement noise, at the level of the growth plate itself?
gap_contradictions.why_it_matters: Saltation implies a switch that can arrest and restart the entire chondrocyte differentiation cascade synchronously across all plates within a day. No such switch is known, and its existence would reframe growth-hormone pharmacodynamics, catch-up growth and the interpretation of any short-interval auxological endpoint (including knemometry endpoints used in inhaled-corticosteroid safety trials).
gap_contradictions.what_is_known: Lampl et al. 1992 reported 0.5-2.5 cm saltations in infant length separated by 2-63 day stasis intervals, with 90-95% of days growth-free (lampl1992). Klein et al. 1994 measured rabbit proximal tibial elongation directly, with ~15-fold better precision than human anthropometry, and found a single Gaussian distribution of daily velocities — continuous, not bimodal (klein1994). Heinrichs et al. 1995 published a further critique (heinrichs1995). Johnson et al. 1996 showed by simulation that frequency-distribution shape cannot exclude saltation (johnson1996). Hermanussen 1998 reported chaotic mini growth spurts in rat rather than true stasis (hermanussen1998). McBrien et al. 2011 reported that canine proximal tibial growth follows saltation and stasis (mcbrien2011). Noonan et al. 2004 showed with implanted microtransducers that at least 90% of lamb tibial elongation happens during recumbency, giving a real, mechanically gated discontinuity on a diurnal timescale (noonan2004).
gap_contradictions.what_is_missing: A measurement in the same species and with the same instrument that can distinguish (i) diurnal load-gated discontinuity, which is established, from (ii) multi-day stasis with a true zero, which is contested. The two camps have never measured the same preparation.
gap_contradictions.nearest_evidence_note: klein1994 (rabbit, continuous), noonan2004 (lamb, load-gated diurnal), lampl1992 and mcbrien2011 (saltatory), hermanussen1998 (chaotic mini-spurts).
gap_contradictions.discriminating_experiment: Implant the Noonan/Wilsman microtransducer across a lamb or rabbit proximal tibial physis and record continuously for 30 days while simultaneously (a) logging posture and (b) delivering weekly fluorochrome labels. Analyse velocity after regressing out posture. If posture-corrected velocity still contains multi-day intervals with velocity indistinguishable from zero and a bimodal distribution, saltation is real at the tissue level; if the posture-corrected residual is unimodal Gaussian, saltation is a compound of load gating and anthropometric measurement error.

gap_contradictions.question: Are the five published skeletal stem cell schemes - mSSC, PTHrP+/FoxA2+ resting chondrocytes, Grem1+ OCR cells, LepR+ stroma and CTSK-lineage periosteal stem cells - distinct cell types, overlapping states of one lineage, or artefacts of different assays?
gap_contradictions.why_it_matters: Downstream layers need to know which cell to target and which mouse model reports on human biology. The schemes disagree on anatomy, adipogenic potential, developmental window and markers, and one immunophenotype (CD200+CD105-Thy-6C3-) is used for two anatomically different 'stem cells'. Without reconciliation, any therapeutic inference from this layer is arbitrary.
gap_contradictions.what_is_known: mSSC is CD45-Ter119-Tie2-AlphaV+Thy-6C3-CD105-CD200+ and excludes fat (chan2015); the periosteal stem cell carries the same CD200+CD105-Thy-6C3- phenotype but is Ctsk-lineage and periosteal (debnath2018); Grem1+ OCR cells are metaphyseal, non-adipogenic and non-overlapping with Nestin-GFP cells (worthley2015); LepR+ cells are perisinusoidal, make adipocytes, contribute nothing to developing cartilage and become the dominant osteoblast source only after adolescence (zhou2014, shu2021); PTHrP+ resting chondrocytes are Grem1-negative (mizuhashi2018); the human CD146+ definition includes adipogenesis (sacchetti2007, bianco2015) while the hSSC definition excludes it and reports CD146+ cells as poorer colony formers (chan2018).
gap_contradictions.what_is_missing: A single study that applies all marker panels and all Cre drivers to the same animals at the same ages with the same functional assay, so that overlap can be measured rather than inferred across papers.
gap_contradictions.discriminating_experiment: Multiplexed intersectional fate mapping in one mouse cohort: combine Pthlh-creER, Grem1-creER, Lepr-cre, Ctsk-cre and FoxA2-creER with orthogonal recombinases and distinct reporters, plus full mSSC/PSC surface staining, sampling at P6, P12, P28 and 12 weeks, and score anatomical position, marker phenotype and clonal output for each labelled cell. Under the 'distinct cell types' model, reporters remain mutually exclusive at all ages and each maps to one compartment. Under the 'states of one lineage' model, early labelled cells convert between reporter identities with age in a directional sequence. Under the 'assay artefact' model, surface phenotype fails to predict clonal output within any single Cre lineage.
gap_contradictions.nearest_evidence_note: mizuhashi2018 is the only cross-scheme quantification located: it measures overlap between PTHrP+ resting chondrocytes and the mSSC/pre-BCSP/BCSP tiers and excludes Grem1 co-expression.

gap_contradictions.question: Does raising bulk cGMP in growth plate cartilage increase longitudinal bone growth? Rat and mouse pharmacology give opposite answers.
gap_contradictions.why_it_matters: The premise of every cGMP-raising growth therapy - CNP analogues, NPR3 decoys, PDE inhibitors - is that more cGMP means more growth. One well-controlled rodent experiment raised growth plate cGMP by half and produced no growth at all, which if generalised means the relevant variable is not bulk cGMP but a compartmentalised pool.
gap_contradictions.what_is_known: In one-month-old rats, tadalafil at 10 mg/kg/day for 3 weeks raised tissue cGMP by 52% and peak CNP-stimulated chondrocyte cGMP by 37%, yet produced no change in long bone length, cortical or trabecular properties or growth plate histology (wang2018). In mouse, PDE3 inhibitors raised chondrocyte cGMP, activated PKG-dependent K+ channels, promoted TRPM7-mediated Ca2+ entry, elongated cultured bones and enlarged juvenile animals (kawabe2025, miyazaki2022). Genetic elevation of NPR2 output raises bone length in mouse (wagner2021, shuhaibar2017).
gap_contradictions.what_is_missing: No experiment resolves whether the discrepancy is species (rat versus mouse), isoform (PDE5 versus PDE3B), compartment (bulk versus microdomain cGMP), or dose/duration. No study has measured subcellular cGMP microdomains in chondrocytes.
gap_contradictions.discriminating_experiment: Run the identical protocol - tadalafil and cilostazol, matched to equal whole-tissue cGMP elevation measured by ELISA - side by side in rat and mouse of the same age, with tibial length by microCT and growth plate zone morphometry as the primary endpoints, and with a targeted cGMP FRET biosensor expressed at the plasma membrane versus in the cytosol to read compartment-specific cGMP. Prediction under the microdomain hypothesis: PDE3 inhibition raises membrane-proximal cGMP and growth in both species while PDE5 inhibition raises only cytosolic cGMP and grows neither. Prediction under a species hypothesis: both drugs grow mouse and neither grows rat.

gap_contradictions.question: Which downstream branch of FGFR3 - MAPK/ERK or STAT1 - carries the load in HUMAN achondroplasia and thanatophoric dysplasia, given that human dysplastic chondrocytes do not show the proliferation defect the STAT1 model predicts?
gap_contradictions.why_it_matters: Every FGFR3-directed drug programme picks a branch. CNP analogues and MEK-directed approaches target MAPK; JAK/STAT-directed approaches target STAT1. If the human lesion is apoptosis-and-differentiation rather than proliferation arrest, then mouse-derived proliferation endpoints are the wrong preclinical readout.
gap_contradictions.what_is_known: In rat chondrosarcoma cells and primary murine chondrocytes, FGF inhibits proliferation through STAT1 and Stat1-null metatarsals do not arrest (sahni1999); the TD II K650E mutant constitutively activates STAT1 (su1997). In mouse, constitutively active MEK1 reproduces achondroplasia-like dwarfism with blocked hypertrophy and NORMAL proliferation, and deleting Stat1 in achondroplasia-mutant mice restores proliferation but rescues neither the reduced hypertrophic zone nor the dwarfism (murakami2004). In cultured human thanatophoric dysplasia type I fetal chondrocytes, mitogenic response to FGF2 and FGF9 was NOT reduced relative to controls; the observed lesion was ligand-independent STAT activation with nuclear STAT1 in hypertrophic cells and increased apoptosis with raised BAX and reduced BCL-2 (legeaimallet1998).
gap_contradictions.what_is_missing: No study measures proliferation index, phospho-ERK and phospho-STAT1 together, in situ and by zone, in human achondroplasia or thanatophoric dysplasia growth plate against age-matched controls. The human and mouse literatures have never been placed on the same measurement.
gap_contradictions.discriminating_experiment: Multiplex immunofluorescence (Ki-67 or phospho-histone H3, phospho-ERK1/2, phospho-STAT1 Y701, cleaved caspase-3, COL10A1) on archival human fetal thanatophoric dysplasia and postnatal achondroplasia growth plate sections with age-matched non-dysplastic controls, quantified per zone. Prediction under the MAPK-dominant model: phospho-ERK is elevated across the prehypertrophic/hypertrophic boundary, COL10A1 domain is compressed, and proliferation index is unchanged. Prediction under the STAT1-dominant model: phospho-STAT1 and cleaved caspase-3 are elevated and proliferation index is reduced in the proliferative zone.

gap_contradictions.question: Is the absence of apoptosis in the fusing human growth plate a real species or process difference, or an artefact of a single specimen?
gap_contradictions.why_it_matters: Apoptosis of terminal hypertrophic chondrocytes is the textbook account of how cartilage is cleared during endochondral ossification, and it is the account carried into fusion by default. The only direct human test of it at fusion is negative. Either the textbook is wrong for the fusion step in humans, or the one available human specimen is unrepresentative. Both possibilities have large downstream consequences for how the atlas grades every apoptosis-based rodent result.
gap_contradictions.what_is_known: In the one human growth plate reported as about to fuse, there was not a single TUNEL-positive cell, cleaved caspase-3 was not detected, and electron microscopy showed no apoptosis or autophagy but did show hypoxia and necrosis; unfused plates contained a few TUNEL-positive chondrocytes (emons2009, human). Independently, estrogen-accelerated loss of rabbit resting-zone chondrocytes also did not appear to be apoptotic (nilsson2014_2, rabbit). Against this, apoptosis of hypertrophic chondrocytes is a well-replicated feature of normal endochondral growth in rodents.
gap_contradictions.what_is_missing: Replication in a second human fusing plate, and a positive control demonstrating that the TUNEL assay used would have detected apoptosis had it been present in that tissue block. No modern death-modality markers (RIPK3, MLKL, GSDMD, LC3/p62) have been applied to any human physeal specimen.
gap_contradictions.discriminating_experiment: Model system: staged human physeal specimens (g_l7fuse_002) and rabbit plates at matched stages as a fusing-species control, with DNase-treated sections as TUNEL positive controls on the same slides. Readout: TUNEL, cleaved caspase-3, RIPK3 and phospho-MLKL, LC3 and p62, and pimonidazole or CAIX as a hypoxia marker, scored zone by zone at the bridging front. Expected results - classical apoptosis: caspase-3-positive, TUNEL-positive cells cluster at the front. Regulated necrosis: phospho-MLKL positive, caspase-3 negative. Hypoxic death: hypoxia marker positive with no regulated-death marker, matching the emons2009 ultrastructure. A finding of apoptosis in the rabbit but not the human would establish a genuine species difference at the final step even between two fusing species.

gap_contradictions.question: Why is FGFR3 K650M (SADDAN) survivable when K650E (thanatophoric dysplasia type II) is lethal, despite K650M producing roughly three times the constitutive receptor kinase activity?
gap_contradictions.why_it_matters: This is the single observation that falsifies the simplest model of the whole FGFR3 series - that phenotype severity is a monotonic function of receptor activation strength. If the scalar model is wrong, then drug development premised on 'reduce FGFR3 kinase output' (infigratinib, TYRA-300) is targeting a quantity that does not by itself determine outcome, and the relevant variable is pathway bias, receptor localisation or tissue distribution.
gap_contradictions.what_is_known: Tavormina 1999 measured ~3-fold greater constitutive kinase activity for K650M than for K650E in transient transfection, and reported four unrelated K650M individuals surviving past infancy without prolonged life support. Bellus 2000 showed the same codon generates weakly activating alleles (K650N, K650Q) that cause hypochondroplasia-like disease. Wilcox 1998 independently found that K650E growth plates are BETTER preserved than R248C and Y373C plates, a second non-monotonicity in the same series.
gap_contradictions.what_is_missing: No study has compared downstream pathway usage (MAPK/ERK vs STAT1 vs PLCgamma), receptor trafficking, or ligand dependence between K650M and K650E in chondrocytes rather than in generic transfected cells. Lethality in thanatophoric dysplasia is respiratory, driven by thoracic cage and cranial base geometry, and no study has asked whether the two alleles differ in their effect on those specific skeletal elements rather than on the long bones.
gap_contradictions.discriminating_experiment: Express K650M and K650E FGFR3 at matched levels in human iPSC-derived chondrocytes and in a costal-cartilage explant model; quantify phospho-ERK, phospho-STAT1 and receptor surface residence, and measure rib and cranial base growth in matched knock-in mouse alleles. Under the scalar model K650M shows uniformly greater signalling and worse growth on every readout; under a pathway-bias model K650M exceeds K650E on ERK but not on STAT1, and STAT1 output tracks the lethal thoracic phenotype.

gap_contradictions.question: Is SOX9 required for chondrocyte hypertrophy, or must SOX9 be downregulated for hypertrophy to occur?
gap_contradictions.why_it_matters: SOX9 is the most convergent node in this layer and the target of every upstream arm. The two published positions imply opposite predictions for any intervention that raises SOX9: one predicts more hypertrophy and faster bone formation, the other predicts a blocked, achondroplasia-like plate. Achondroplasia therapeutics reasoning depends on which is correct.
gap_contradictions.what_is_known: Dy 2012 shows, using doxycycline-inducible Cre and Sox9 conditional nulls in mouse, that SOX9 is REQUIRED to maintain columnar proliferation and to generate hypertrophy, that SOX9 protein outlives its mRNA into upper hypertrophic cells, and that it acts there with MEF2C to directly activate Col10a1. Zhou 2015 shows that activated mutant FGFR3 impairs endochondral growth by PREVENTING SOX9 downregulation in differentiating chondrocytes, i.e. persistent SOX9 is the lesion. Kohn 2015 adds that prolonged Notch signalling suppresses Sox9 and that this suppression is required for the onset of maturation.
gap_contradictions.what_is_missing: No experiment titrates SOX9 level within a single differentiating chondrocyte population and measures hypertrophy as a continuous function of it. The two positions may be reconciled by a biphasic requirement (SOX9 needed to license Col10a1 but needing to fall for terminal maturation), but that reconciliation has not been tested.
gap_contradictions.discriminating_experiment: A degron-tagged endogenous SOX9 allele in mouse or human chondrocytes allowing graded, reversible protein reduction, applied at defined points along the differentiation trajectory, with live readout of COL10A1 reporter and cell volume. Under the "required" hypothesis, reducing SOX9 at the prehypertrophic step lowers COL10A1 monotonically. Under the "must fall" hypothesis, modest reduction at that step raises COL10A1 and accelerates volume increase. A biphasic curve with a maximum at intermediate SOX9 supports the reconciliation and gives the field a set point.

gap_contradictions.question: Do static and dynamic loading at equal mean stress suppress growth rate equally, or is dynamic loading growth-sparing?
gap_contradictions.why_it_matters: The claim that dynamic loading preserves growth where static suppresses it is the stated rationale for cyclically controlled vertebral tethers and for 'physiological' growth-modulation implants. If dynamic loading suppresses growth just as much and only spares the tissue, then such devices will still stunt the segment they are applied to, and the design goal should be tissue preservation, not growth preservation.
gap_contradictions.what_is_known: Duty cycle matters: reducing 0.1 MPa compression from 24 to 12 h/day raised rat vertebral growth from 82% to 90-93% of control and tibial growth from 70% to 84-86% (stokes2005). Waveform apparently does not: sinusoidal 0.2 MPa +/-30% at 0.1 Hz reduced rat caudal vertebral growth by the same 19% as sustained 0.2 MPa, while sparing plate thickness, proliferative cells per column and hypertrophic cell height (valteau2011). Explants tell the tissue-sparing half of the story (sergerie2011, kaviani2015) and cell-strain measurements give the viscoelastic explanation (zimmermann2017). Frost's chondral modeling theory predicts the opposite of the valteau2011 result (frost1979).
gap_contradictions.what_is_missing: A single experiment that varies duty cycle and waveform orthogonally at matched mean stress with a growth-rate endpoint, so that 'intermittent' (load off part of the day) and 'dynamic' (oscillating about a non-zero mean) are not conflated, as they routinely are in reviews.
gap_contradictions.discriminating_experiment: Rat caudal vertebra, 2x3 factorial, n>=8 per cell: duty cycle 24 h/day vs 12 h/day, crossed with waveform sustained, 0.1 Hz sinusoid and 1.0 Hz sinusoid, all at 0.2 MPa time-averaged stress, 14 days, fluorochrome growth rate plus histomorphometry. Under the growth-sparing hypothesis, waveform has a main effect on growth rate. Under the mean-stress hypothesis, only duty cycle affects growth rate while waveform affects only histomorphometry, which is what valteau2011 and stokes2005 jointly imply.

gap_contradictions.question: Which thyroid hormone receptor isoform mediates T3 action in growth plate chondrocytes - TRalpha, as human THRA mutations imply, or TRbeta, as mouse rib chondrocyte knockouts imply?
gap_contradictions.why_it_matters: Isoform-selective thyromimetics (resmetirom-class TRbeta agonists) are entering clinical use, and their skeletal safety in growing children depends entirely on which isoform the plate uses. If the plate is TRbeta-driven, a TRbeta-selective agonist would accelerate hypertrophic differentiation and advance bone age; if TRalpha-driven, the same drug would be skeletally silent. The literature currently supports both answers.
gap_contradictions.what_is_known: Human side - heterozygous dominant-negative THRA variants cause growth retardation, delayed bone age and disharmonious short stature with low free T4 and normal-to-mildly- raised TSH, and these children respond to levothyroxine plus rhGH with height gains up to 2.5 SDS (jorge2025). Human RTHbeta (dominant-negative THRB) is common, well described and typically NOT associated with short stature. Mouse side - in primary neonatal rib chondrocytes, T3 reduced proliferation and accelerated differentiation normally in TRalpha-deficient cells but ALL T3 responses were abolished in TRbeta-deficient cells, and T3 upregulated TRbeta1 itself (rabier2006). Both TRalpha1, TRalpha2 and TRbeta1 protein are present in rat reserve and proliferating zone chondrocytes and absent from hypertrophic cells (robson2000), so localisation does not adjudicate.
gap_contradictions.what_is_missing: No isoform-selective test in long-bone growth plate chondrocytes of either species - the mouse experiment used RIB chondrocytes, a different skeletal element - and no measurement of THRA versus THRB transcript or protein in human physeal tissue. Germline knockouts also permit compensation that a conditional, adult-onset deletion would not.
gap_contradictions.discriminating_experiment: Model system - side-by-side conditional deletion of Thra and Thrb in Acan-CreERT2 chondrocytes of the mouse proximal tibia, induced postnatally, plus primary human growth plate chondrocytes from surgical waste treated with isoform-selective agonists (TRbeta-selective resmetirom-class compound versus a TRalpha-sparing control) at matched receptor occupancy. Readout - tibial length and zonal heights in vivo; COL10A1, ALPL and proliferation index in the human cells; isoform transcript quantification in the same human tissue. Expected result - under the human-genetics-led model, Thra deletion shortens the tibia and TRbeta-selective agonists leave human chondrocyte differentiation markers unchanged; under the mouse-chondrocyte-led model, Thrb deletion is the one that blocks hypertrophic differentiation and the TRbeta agonist induces COL10A1 in human cells - which would be a direct paediatric safety signal for that drug class.

gap_contradictions.question: What drives the seasonal variation in human height velocity - photoperiod, ambient temperature, or seasonal nutrition - and why does the phase of the peak differ between cohorts?
gap_contradictions.why_it_matters: The seasonal amplitude is not trivial (~13% of mean linear growth velocity in infants), which means growth-velocity measurement intervals shorter than a year are systematically biased by season - directly affecting clinical decisions about starting or stopping GH and the interpretation of short trials. It is also the only routinely observable environmental modulator of the human growth plate, so identifying the transducer would be mechanistically valuable.
gap_contradictions.what_is_known: Three large human cohorts agree that seasonality is real and disagree on phase and driver. In 11,587 three-month intervals from 2,277 GH-treated prepubertal children, height velocity scaled with average daylight hours (+0.146 cm/yr per hour in treatment year 1, +0.121 thereafter), the effect grew with latitude, and calendar month had no independent effect - a photoperiod signature (shulman2013). In 9,409 Japanese infants, length z-velocity peaked in SUMMER, with a winter-summer difference of 0.0026 z/day (95% CI 0.0015-0.0036), about 13% of mean velocity (narumi2020). In 760 Danish 8-11 year olds, height velocity was above the 6.10 cm/yr mean in JANUARY-APRIL, and unlike earlier reports of a spring height peak with an autumn weight peak, weight, BMI and fat-free mass index peaked coincidentally (dalskov2016).
gap_contradictions.what_is_missing: No study manipulates photoperiod, temperature or energy intake independently while measuring growth, and no study measures a candidate mediator (melatonin amplitude, 25-hydroxyvitamin D, IGF-1, GH pulsatility) longitudinally across seasons in the same children with growth as the outcome. The competing explanations have never been placed in one model.
gap_contradictions.discriminating_experiment: Model system - a prospective cohort of prepubertal children measured by knemometry every 2 weeks for 24 months at three widely separated latitudes (for example ~60 N, ~35 N and ~5 N), with a nested arm in a controlled-photoperiod setting (polar winter workers' children or a residential facility with fixed lighting). Readout - lower-leg length velocity as the outcome, with monthly serum 25(OH)D, IGF-1, IGFBP-3, overnight urinary 6-sulphatoxymelatonin and 7-day dietary energy record as candidate mediators, analysed by mediation model. Expected result - under a photoperiod model, growth velocity amplitude scales with latitude, peaks in phase with daylight hours regardless of temperature, and melatonin amplitude is the strongest mediator; under a temperature/energy model, amplitude tracks seasonal temperature or energy intake and is near zero at low latitude despite a substantial photoperiod swing there being absent; under a vitamin D model, 25(OH)D mediates the effect and supplementation in a randomised sub-arm abolishes the seasonal amplitude.

gap_contradictions.question: Why does pharmacological glucocorticoid act locally and potently on the growth plate (77% growth suppression on unilateral infusion in rabbit) while genetic deletion of the glucocorticoid receptor from chondrocytes leaves mouse growth plates and long bone length entirely normal?
gap_contradictions.why_it_matters: These two results are used interchangeably to support "glucocorticoids act on the chondrocyte", but they cannot both mean that. Either the receptor mediating pharmacological suppression is not the classical chondrocyte GR (raising the possibility of a perichondrial, vascular or mineralocorticoid-receptor route), or endogenous and pharmacological glucocorticoid exposures engage different mechanisms. The answer changes what a growth-sparing steroid would have to avoid.
gap_contradictions.what_is_known: Local intra-plate dexamethasone infusion (80 ng/uL at 1 uL/h) reduced ipsilateral rabbit proximal tibial growth by 77% versus the vehicle-infused contralateral plate, P<0.0001, with a measurement error of ~5% (baron1992); subsequent catch-up was likewise confined to the treated plate (baron1994); dexamethasone slowed rabbit resting zone chondrocyte proliferation and their numerical depletion (schrier2006). Against this, tamoxifen- inducible chondrocyte-specific GR knockout mice showed normal knee joint architecture, cartilage structure, growth plates, intervertebral discs, long bone length and bone microarchitecture at all ages, with a defect confined to metaphyseal fracture healing (tu2014).
gap_contradictions.what_is_missing: No experiment applies the two designs to the same question: nobody has performed the unilateral local dexamethasone infusion in a chondrocyte-specific GR knockout animal, which is the single measurement that would resolve it. Nor has the mouse GR knockout been challenged with systemic glucocorticoid excess and a growth endpoint.
gap_contradictions.discriminating_experiment: Model system - Acan-CreERT2 x Nr3c1-flox mice and littermate controls, each receiving unilateral intra-growth-plate dexamethasone infusion with contralateral vehicle, plus a systemic high-dose dexamethasone arm. Readout - ipsilateral versus contralateral tibial growth rate by calcein/tetracycline double labelling and pin-radiograph measurement, with zonal heights and resting zone chondrocyte counts. Expected result - under a chondrocyte-GR model, local dexamethasone suppresses growth in controls but has no ipsilateral effect in chondrocyte-GR-null mice, and the mouse null result in tu2014 is simply the absence of a physiological ligand challenge; under a non-chondrocyte-target model, local dexamethasone suppresses growth equally in both genotypes, redirecting the search to perichondrium, hypertrophic-zone vasculature or the mineralocorticoid receptor.

gap_contradictions.question: Does ANKH export inorganic pyrophosphate directly from growth plate chondrocytes, or does it export ATP that ENPP1 then converts to PPi extracellularly?
gap_contradictions.why_it_matters: The two models predict opposite consequences for any intervention. If ANKH exports PPi, then ANKH activity alone sets local PPi and ENPP1 is a parallel source. If ANKH exports ATP, then ENPP1 is obligatorily downstream of ANKH, no ANKH-derived PPi exists without ENPP1, and purinergic signalling through the exported ATP is an unrecognised second output of the same transporter - relevant because extracellular ATP acts on P2 receptors on chondrocytes. The entire growth plate ANK literature was interpreted under the first model.
gap_contradictions.what_is_known: Under the PPi-transport model: blocking Ank transport or expression in terminally differentiated mineralizing growth plate chondrocytes raises intra- AND extracellular PPi, lowers alkaline phosphatase and blocks mineralization, and Ank overexpression in hypertrophic non-mineralizing chondrocytes lowers intra- and extracellular PPi and induces mineralization (wang2005); ANK expression is HIF-1 and oxygen dependent in these cells (zaka2009). Under the ATP-export model: ANKH introduced into ENPP1-knockout HEK293 cells produces robust ATP release with NO rise in extracellular PPi, Enpp1-/- mouse bone contains under 2.5% of wild-type PPi despite intact Ank, and ANKH supplies about 25% of plasma PPi with ABCC6 supplying 60-70%, both by NTP efflux (szeri2022). Consistently, NPP1 but not ANK localises to matrix vesicles (harmey2004).
gap_contradictions.what_is_missing: The decisive experiment has been done in HEK293 overexpression, not in chondrocytes. No study has tested ANK function in growth plate chondrocytes lacking ENPP1.
gap_contradictions.discriminating_experiment: Generate Enpp1-null primary growth plate chondrocytes (from Enpp1-/- mice or by CRISPR in a chondrocytic line), then overexpress or silence Ank and measure extracellular ATP by luciferase and extracellular PPi by the ATP-sulfurylase assay (lundkvist2023) in parallel, with matched Enpp1-intact controls. Under the ATP-export model, Ank manipulation will change extracellular ATP in both genotypes but change extracellular PPi only in Enpp1-intact cells, and the mineralization phenotype of wang2005 will be abolished in the Enpp1-null background. Under the PPi-transport model, Ank manipulation will change extracellular PPi in both genotypes. Add an apyrase control to confirm that any PPi rise depends on released ATP.

gap_contradictions.question: Which zone of the growth plate is stiffest, and does the direction of the zonal stiffness gradient depend on species, anatomical site, or measurement method?
gap_contradictions.why_it_matters: Physeal fractures propagate through a mechanically weak plane, and guided-growth and distraction hardware are designed around assumed stiffness gradients. The published gradients point in different directions, so the predicted failure plane and the predicted strain distribution across the plate differ between studies that are all cited interchangeably.
gap_contradictions.what_is_known: Newborn porcine distal ulna, unconfined compression, transversely isotropic biphasic model: the RESERVE zone is stiffest, with PZ and HZ half as stiff axially and about a third as stiff transversely, and three times as permeable radially (sergerie2009). Nine-week rabbit proximal tibia, microindentation: modulus PEAKS in the UPPER HYPERTROPHIC zone, range 380-690 kPa, with proteoglycan content correlating with compressive modulus (eckstein2022). Rabbit cranial base, AFM microindentation: modulus increases MONOTONICALLY from reserve (0.57 MPa) to mineralizing zone (1.41 MPa) (radhakrishnan2004). Human phalangeal and tibial growth plate, sharp-tip AFM: HZ (416 MPa) stiffer than RZ (131 MPa) (xie2025). Bovine tensile failure runs from the upper columnar into the reserve zone, leaving chondrons intact on the metaphyseal side (williams2001).
gap_contradictions.what_is_missing: A single study measuring more than one species, more than one anatomical site and more than one method on comparable tissue. The five datasets differ simultaneously in species, site (weight-bearing long bone versus cranial base versus phalanx), age, hydration, loading mode and constitutive model, so no variable can be isolated.
gap_contradictions.discriminating_experiment: A single-laboratory factorial study: proximal tibial and cranial base physes from rabbit and pig at two ages, each specimen measured by (i) microindentation with a 100 um spherical probe, (ii) AFM with a 5 um spherical probe, and (iii) zone-dissected unconfined compression, all hydrated in PBS, with paired Safranin-O and Raman proteoglycan mapping. If the gradient direction is method-dependent, indentation and compression will disagree within the same specimen and the field's disagreement is an artefact of technique. If it is site-dependent, cranial base and long bone will differ consistently across methods and species, and cranial-base data (radhakrishnan2004) should be excluded from long-bone models. If it is age-dependent, the newborn porcine result (reserve stiffest) will reverse in older animals as the hypertrophic zone begins to calcify.

gap_contradictions.question: Is the difference in elongation rate between long and short bones dominated by chondrocyte hypertrophic volume or by proliferation per column?
gap_contradictions.why_it_matters: The two answers point at different biology and different drugs. If final hypertrophic volume dominates, the target is the IGF-dependent swelling phase and the matrix conditions that permit it (L5). If proliferation per column dominates, the target is the resting zone's output and the senescence programme that limits it (L2). The atlas cannot carry both as the headline mechanism of skeletal proportion.
gap_contradictions.what_is_known: cooper2013 used quantitative phase microscopy to show three phases of chondrocyte volume increase and reported that the duration of the third, IGF-dependent, proportional-dry-mass phase is what varies most between rapidly and slowly elongating growth plates, concluding that the largest contribution to differential elongation comes from hypertrophic volume. lui2018 measured both variables in the same animals and found the opposite ranking: at one week the metacarpal grew at 49% of the tibial rate with proliferation per column at 46% of tibial, while hypertrophic cell height differed little at that timepoint, and concluded that proliferation per column is the dominant factor. Both are mouse; both are competent; they disagree.
gap_contradictions.what_is_missing: A reconciliation. The two studies differ in the ages examined, in the bones compared and in whether volume was measured as height or as true volume with dry-mass correction, and neither reanalyses the other's data. The L1 node site_specific_growth_rate records a third position from rat, that eight chondrocytic variables contribute and the relative share of hypertrophy falls from 59% to 44% as plates get slower, which suggests the answer is age- and rate-dependent rather than fixed.
gap_contradictions.discriminating_experiment: A single study measuring, in the same mice at four ages spanning 1 to 6 weeks, and at four sites (distal femur, proximal tibia, metacarpal, proximal phalanx): elongation rate by calcein labelling, proliferation per column by EdU, and terminal hypertrophic cell VOLUME by quantitative phase microscopy rather than section height. Then partition the between-site variance in rate into the two components at each age. The prediction that reconciles both papers is that proliferation per column dominates early and hypertrophic volume dominates late; if instead one component dominates at every age, one of the two published conclusions is wrong.

gap_contradictions.question: Does infigratinib inhibit the FGFR3-N540K hypochondroplasia mutant potently enough to be therapeutic, or is it a weak inhibitor of that specific allele?
gap_contradictions.why_it_matters: Hypochondroplasia is the declared next indication for infigratinib and a phase 2 programme is predicated on the affirmative answer. Two groups in the same journal within months give opposite answers about the same drug against the same mutant. If the negative report is right, a trial is being designed on an allele the drug does not adequately engage, and any null result will be misread as evidence against FGFR3 inhibition in general rather than against this compound at this allele.
gap_contradictions.what_is_known: Demuynck 2025 reports in silico strong interaction, potent in vitro inhibition, and significant skeletal improvement in Fgfr3-N534K/+ mice. Ursachi 2026 reports that infigratinib is a weak inhibitor of FGFR3-N540K. An independent kinase panel shows infigratinib potency varies ~89-fold between K650E and K650M, establishing that strong allele-dependence of this compound is real.
gap_contradictions.what_is_missing: A single head-to-head biochemical comparison of infigratinib against wild-type, G380R, N540K and N540K-equivalent mouse N534K FGFR3 in one assay with stated ATP concentration, plus a matched cellular assay.
gap_contradictions.discriminating_experiment: Run all four FGFR3 variants side by side in a single laboratory using a microfluidic mobility-shift kinase assay at ATP = Km and again at 1 mM ATP, paired with a BaF3 TEL-FGFR3 proliferation assay for each variant. THERAPEUTIC - N540K IC50 within ~3-fold of wild-type at both ATP concentrations and cellular IC50 below achievable free plasma concentration at 0.25 mg/kg/day. NOT THERAPEUTIC - N540K IC50 >20-fold weaker, in which case the hypochondroplasia programme needs a different compound.

gap_contradictions.question: Which is correct for clinical use, the +/-8.5 cm target-height band derived theoretically by Tanner, or the +/-1.64 SDS band (+/-10.6 cm girls, +/-11.7 cm boys) recommended by the growth hormone societies, given a measured residual SD of 4.4-4.7 cm?
gap_contradictions.why_it_matters: These are two different thresholds for the same clinical decision and they differ by up to 3.2 cm at the boundary. A child 10 cm below target height has a 1.0-1.5% prior probability of that deviation under the measured SD, which is inside the guideline band but outside the Tanner band. The discrepancy determines who is investigated and who is treated.
gap_contradictions.what_is_known: The +/-8.5 cm band was derived from theoretical considerations as the 3rd-to-97th centile band, not measured, and was later revised by its own authors to +/-9 cm for girls and +/-10 cm for boys (documented in zeevi2024, citing tanner1970). The +/-1.64 SDS band recommended by the GH Research Society, LWPES and ESPE converts under CDC standards to +/-10.6 and +/-11.7 cm (zeevi2024). The directly measured residual SD is 4.7 cm (sons) and 4.4 cm (daughters), which corresponds to a 95% band of about +/-9.2 and +/-8.6 cm.
gap_contradictions.what_is_missing: No published reconciliation. The guideline band and the empirical SD have not been compared in a paper that both cohorts' authors would accept, and no study has tested which threshold better separates children with a subsequently identified pathological cause of short stature from those without.
gap_contradictions.discriminating_experiment: Model system: a retrospective cohort of children referred for short stature with measured parental heights, complete diagnostic workup and eventual diagnosis (pathological versus familial/constitutional). Readout: sensitivity and specificity for a pathological diagnosis of the three candidate thresholds (+/-8.5 cm, +/-1.64 SDS, +/-2 SD of the measured 4.4-4.7 cm residual), with the corrected target height in all three cases. Expected result if the empirical SD is right: the narrow threshold has materially higher sensitivity at acceptable specificity, and the guideline band is missing pathology. Expected result if the guideline is right: the narrow threshold produces an unacceptable false-positive rate without gaining sensitivity, implying the empirical SD is cohort-specific.

gap_contradictions.question: Does muscle growth cause bone mineral accrual during the pubertal spurt, or are the two independently determined and merely correlated in time?
gap_contradictions.why_it_matters: Peak lean mass velocity precedes and statistically predicts peak bone mineral content velocity at every anatomical site while peak height velocity does not, which is read as support for the mechanostat. The authors of the primary explicitly state their data cannot exclude independent genetic determination of both. The two readings imply opposite intervention strategies for bone accrual in childhood.
gap_contradictions.what_is_known: Peak lean mass velocity precedes peak bone mineral content velocity by 0.36 y (boys) and 0.51 y (girls) for the total body, 0.63 and 0.71 y in the arms, and 0.48 and 0.22 y in the legs; peak lean mass velocity explains 41-61% of the variance in regional peak bone mineral content velocity while peak height velocity and sex explain none independently (rauch2004). The lag differs three-fold between the arms of boys and the legs of girls, which a single systemic driver does not predict.
gap_contradictions.what_is_missing: Any intervention that changes muscle mass without changing hormonal status during growth and measures bone accrual, and any genetically informed decomposition (twin or polygenic score) of the lean mass to bone mineral relationship in growing children.
gap_contradictions.discriminating_experiment: Model system: a unilateral loading paradigm in growing adolescents - for example the dominant versus non-dominant arm in racquet sport players, who differ in muscle mass within the same endocrine environment. Readout: side-to-side difference in lean mass velocity and in bone mineral content velocity measured longitudinally through the spurt. Expected result if muscle causes bone: the within-person side difference in lean mass velocity predicts the side difference in bone mineral velocity with the same lag as the between-person relationship. Expected result if both are independently determined: side differences in lean mass appear without a corresponding lagged bone response beyond the known direct loading effect on cortical geometry.

gap_contradictions.question: Does the growth plate phenotype of a chondrocyte-specific cGKI/cGKII (Prkg1;Prkg2) double knockout phenocopy CNP or GC-B loss - a thinned plate with a hypertrophic layer reduced to roughly a quarter of control - or does it reproduce the EXPANDED plate of the cGKII single mutant?
gap_contradictions.why_it_matters: The atlas, and every review of CNP signalling, wires CNP through GC-B and cGMP to PKG-II as a linear chain. That chain makes a falsifiable prediction: losing the terminal kinase should phenocopy losing the receptor. It does the opposite. The cartilage-specific Npr2 knockout hypertrophic layer is 23.0% of control with a thinner plate overall (nakao2015), while the Prkg2-mutant KMI rat plate is 2.6-fold EXPANDED, 665 +/- 47 versus 255 +/- 34 um, n=8 (chikuda2004). Until this is resolved, no quantitative model of the CNP arm - including any model used to reason about vosoritide dose-response - has a validated effector step.
gap_contradictions.what_is_known: Prkg2 loss expands the plate through an accumulated intermediate layer of postmitotic, ALP-negative, collagen X-negative chondrocytes (chikuda2004); Npr2 or Nppc loss shrinks it (nakao2015). cGKI (Prkg1) is co-expressed in the same compartment at HIGHER zonal enrichment than cGKII - 5.9-fold versus 4.4-fold by micro-dissection microarray (agoston2007). Both chikuda2004 and agoston2007 independently name cGKI as the unexcluded alternative and both propose the double knockout as the resolving experiment. PKG also has at least one substrate arm outside SOX9/GSK-3beta: chondrocyte-specific Trpm7 ablation abolishes CNP-driven bone growth via a PKG-BK channel-TRPM7-CaMKII route (miyazaki2022).
gap_contradictions.what_is_missing: The double knockout has not been made in cartilage, in any species, in the 22 years since it was first proposed. No study has measured cGKI protein by zone in growth plate. No study has asked which of the two kinases carries the Trpm7-dependent arm.
gap_contradictions.discriminating_experiment: Generate Col2a1-Cre;Prkg1(fl/fl);Prkg2(fl/fl) mice alongside each single conditional and a Col2a1-Cre;Npr2(fl/fl) control, all on one background, and measure proximal tibial growth plate total height, type X collagen-positive hypertrophic layer height and BrdU index at 2 weeks. Prediction if cGKI compensates within a single linear chain: the double knockout thins the plate and reduces the hypertrophic layer toward the Npr2-knockout value (~23% of control), resolving the sign conflict. Prediction if PKG-II acts on a separate proliferation-to-hypertrophy switch that is not the route by which CNP promotes growth: the double knockout retains or worsens the EXPANDED postmitotic non-hypertrophic intermediate layer, which would mean the CNP growth signal reaches the plate through an effector other than either cGK - the Trpm7 arm being the leading candidate.

gap_contradictions.question: Do achondroplasia and thanatophoric FGFR3 mutants show INCREASED or DECREASED c-Cbl-mediated ubiquitination, and does the answer depend on the cell background or on the ligand-exposure regime?
gap_contradictions.why_it_matters: The failed-termination arm of achondroplasia pathogenesis rests on this sign. If mutant FGFR3 is under-ubiquitinated it escapes lysosomal degradation, which is the model in the atlas and in reviews. If it is over-ubiquitinated the receptor accumulates for a different reason and the therapeutic logic of degradation-promoting strategies inverts. The two published answers are opposite and both come from competent labs.
gap_contradictions.what_is_known: cho2004 reports REDUCED ubiquitination of ACH and TDII FGFR3 in Cos-7 and RCJ cells, greater for TDII than ACH, with coexpressed wild-type c-Cbl more than doubling wild-type receptor ubiquitination while having little effect on the mutants. Monsonego-Ornan et al. 2004 report INCREASED ubiquitination. cho2004 names the disparity and attributes it to four differences - Cos-7 versus HEK293, steady-state FGF2 versus 30 min-6 h FGF9, retroviral versus transient expression, and the resulting receptor level - and states it cannot exclude the alternative. c-Cbl recruitment to FGFR is indirect, via FRS2alpha and Grb2, and FRS2alpha binds FGFR1 far more strongly than FGFR3.
gap_contradictions.what_is_missing: No experiment has measured FGFR3 ubiquitination in chondrocytes expressing the receptor from its endogenous locus, which is the only context in which receptor level is not an experimental variable. No study has tested whether the sign flips with expression level within one cell system.
gap_contradictions.discriminating_experiment: In primary rib or growth plate chondrocytes from Fgfr3(G380R/+) knock-in mice and wild-type littermates - endogenous locus, endogenous level - immunoprecipitate FGFR3 and blot for ubiquitin at 0, 15, 60 and 240 min of FGF2, with and without Cbl knockdown, and run the same protocol in parallel at three titrated overexpression levels in HEK293. Prediction under cho2004: mutant/wild-type ubiquitination ratio is below 1 at endogenous level and stays below 1 as expression rises. Prediction if the disparity is an overexpression artefact: the ratio is below 1 at endogenous level and crosses above 1 as the degradation pathway saturates, which would reconcile both papers and retire the contradiction.

gap_contradictions.question: Is the resting-zone division budget that sets growth plate senescence actually finite and conserved across growth-inhibited periods, given that resting-zone chondrocytes acquire self-renewing stem cell behaviour after secondary ossification centre formation?
gap_contradictions.why_it_matters: The finite-capacity model is the atlas's explanation for catch-up growth, for the shape of the human growth velocity curve, and for why growth-inhibiting illness is partly recoverable. If the resting zone self-renews, the budget is not fixed and the model needs a different limiting quantity - niche exhaustion, clonal drift, or matrix change - with different clinical predictions about how much catch-up is recoverable and for how long.
gap_contradictions.what_is_known: marino2008 shows hypothyroidism delays functional, structural and molecular senescence markers in rat, but catch-up growth was statistically INCOMPLETE at final measurement for body mass, tail length and tibia length, and the authors give two explanations that both entail imperfect conservation. That study also suppressed the gonadal axis incompletely (uterine mass ~0.16 g against ~0.1 g ovariectomised, ~0.5 g intact), leaving oestrogen present. Independently, mizuhashi2018 and newton2019 show PTHrP+ resting-zone chondrocytes switch to self-renewing clonal behaviour after secondary ossification centre formation.
gap_contradictions.what_is_missing: No study has measured resting-zone clone number or clone size in a growth-inhibited animal and compared it with an age-matched control at the same body size - which is the measurement the conservation claim asserts. The two literatures have never been run in the same animal.
gap_contradictions.discriminating_experiment: Multicolour clonal lineage tracing (Pthrp-CreER;Confetti) in rats or mice made hypothyroid for 8 weeks and then released, versus untreated age-matched and size-matched controls, scoring resting-zone clone number, clone size and column output at release and at the point of matched body size. Prediction under strict conservation: at MATCHED BODY SIZE the treated and control plates have indistinguishable clone counts and clone sizes - the budget was spent, not aged. Prediction under partial conservation, which is what the incomplete catch-up in marino2008 implies: treated plates show fewer surviving clones or smaller clone output at matched size, quantifying the leak. Include an ovariectomised arm to remove the oestrogen confound that marino2008 could not.

gap_contradictions.question: Does static or dynamic compression at matched mean strain disrupt growth plate columnar architecture? In vivo rat says static; in vitro swine explant says dynamic. Which sign is right, and is the difference explained by explant boundary conditions or by duration?
gap_contradictions.why_it_matters: The entire clinical argument for dynamic rather than static tethering rests on the claim that dynamic loading is architecture-sparing. If the explant result is the correct one, dynamic tethering devices are being designed on an inverted premise.
gap_contradictions.what_is_known: In vivo, rat caudal vertebra at 0.2 MPa mean for 2 weeks: static and dynamic (0.1 Hz, +/-30%) suppressed growth equally (19% each) but only STATIC reduced plate thickness, proliferative cells per column and hypertrophic cell height (p<0.01 static vs dynamic; hypertrophic cell height p=0.014) (valteau2011). In vitro, 4-week-old swine ulnar explants for 48 h at matched mean strain: DYNAMIC (7-13% at 0.1 Hz) caused severe loss of columnar arrangement in proliferative and hypertrophic zones, while STATIC (10%) preserved columns with only slight deviation from the growth axis - and dynamic loading increased aggrecan and collagen II while static depleted them (sergerie2011). Separately, explant chondrocyte viability falls with frequency and amplitude, with proliferative and hypertrophic zones most sensitive (kaviani2015), and static loading produces higher lateral and volumetric hypertrophic cell strain than dynamic at equal mean stress (zimmermann2017).
gap_contradictions.what_is_missing: A single experimental series that applies matched static and dynamic protocols to the same species and site in vivo AND ex vivo, with identical architectural scoring. The two studies differ in species (rat vs swine), site (caudal vertebra vs ulna), duration (2 weeks vs 48 h), loading control (stress vs strain), and boundary conditions (intact vs cut explant), so no single explanation can currently be assigned.
gap_contradictions.discriminating_experiment: Model system: skeletally immature pigs, distal ulnar physis, with one forelimb instrumented for in vivo static compression and the contralateral for dynamic at matched mean stress, plus explants from a third cohort of the same animals loaded in a bioreactor with the identical waveforms for 48 h and for 2 weeks. Readout: blinded column-deviation angle, proliferative cells per column, hypertrophic zone height, and aggrecan/collagen II quantified by immunoblot rather than immunohistochemistry. Expected results - if the discrepancy is a duration artefact, the 48 h explant and 48 h in vivo arms agree with each other and both differ from the 2-week arms; if it is a boundary-condition artefact, the in vivo arms agree at both durations and both explant arms differ; if the sign truly inverts between rodent caudal and large-animal appendicular plates, the pig in vivo arm reproduces the swine explant result and the rat literature is site-specific rather than wrong.

gap_contradictions.question: Do glucocorticoids raise or lower SOX9 in chondrocytes, and does the direction reverse between nanomolar and micromolar concentrations?
gap_contradictions.why_it_matters: SOX9 is the master chondrogenic transcription factor and glucocorticoid excess is the most potent single suppressor of childhood linear growth. If dexamethasone RAISES SOX9 at physiological concentrations, then glucocorticoid growth suppression cannot be explained by loss of chondrogenic identity and must run through IGF-1 resistance, IHH suppression and apoptosis instead. Standard chondrogenic differentiation media contain 100 nM dexamethasone precisely because it is pro-chondrogenic, which is difficult to reconcile with the clinical phenotype.
gap_contradictions.what_is_known: Dexamethasone enhanced Sox9 mRNA and protein in newborn mouse rib chondrocytes within 24 h, threshold 0.1 nM, maximal at 10 nM, with parallel Col2a1 induction and no change in Sox9 mRNA half-life (sekiya2001). Glucocorticoid at 100 uM suppressed SOX9, COL2 and aggrecan in human knee articular chondrocytes, time- and dose-dependently, through p38 inactivation, before any apoptotic effect appeared (song2012).
gap_contradictions.what_is_missing: No study runs a full concentration-response for SOX9 across 0.1 nM to 100 uM in a single cell type, and no study measures SOX9 zonally in a growth plate after in-vivo glucocorticoid exposure at a dose that suppresses growth.
gap_contradictions.discriminating_experiment: Infuse dexamethasone directly into one rabbit proximal tibial growth plate at the 80 ng/uL, 1 uL/h rate shown by baron1992 to cut growth by 77%, with vehicle contralaterally, and quantify SOX9 protein by zonal immunohistochemistry at 7 days, alongside a 6-point concentration-response for SOX9 in the same primary chondrocytes in vitro. Monophasic suppression in vivo would retire the pro-chondrogenic reading; unchanged or raised SOX9 in vivo despite a 77% growth deficit would establish that glucocorticoid growth arrest is not a SOX9 lesion at all.

gap_contradictions.question: Why does androgen receptor modulation have no effect on longitudinal growth in cultured metatarsals when AR protein is present in 41-65% of human growth plate chondrocytes?
gap_contradictions.why_it_matters: Whether androgens act directly on the plate or only after aromatisation to estrogen determines whether non-aromatisable androgens (oxandrolone, DHT) can be used to gain height without advancing bone age, and whether aromatase inhibitors in boys act purely by removing an estrogen brake. The receptor-expression literature and the functional literature currently point in opposite directions.
gap_contradictions.what_is_known: AR is immunolocalised in human growth plate chondrocytes with zonal structure - 65% of resting, 41% of proliferative and 58% of hypertrophic cells positive, with no sex difference and no Tanner-stage trend (nilsson2003) - and in rat tibial growth plate with a sex difference (van2002). Yet neither AR agonism nor AR antagonism altered elongation of cultured fetal rat metatarsals (chagin2009), and testosterone actually INHIBITED proliferation of cultured human growth plate chondrocytes (olney2004). Complete androgen insensitivity syndrome is compatible with a normal female growth spurt.
gap_contradictions.what_is_missing: No chondrocyte-specific Ar deletion has been reported with growth plate morphometry, and no experiment has tested a non-aromatisable androgen on the plate in the presence and absence of aromatase.
gap_contradictions.discriminating_experiment: Generate Col2a1-CreERT2;Ar-flox mice, delete AR in cartilage at P14 in both sexes, and measure tibial elongation rate by calcein double-labelling, zonal heights, and time to growth cessation, with an orchidectomy plus DHT arm to remove the aromatisable substrate. Normal growth and normal fusion timing in cartilage-AR-null males would settle the question in favour of the aromatisation route; a shortened proliferative zone would mean the metatarsal explant assay simply lacks the relevant readout or timeframe.

gap_contradictions.question: Does the Mmp13-null growth plate phenotype persist into adult life or resolve by 12 weeks, and is collagen II cleavage in the lower hypertrophic zone attributable to MMP-13 alone or to MMP-13 acting synergistically with MMP-9?
gap_contradictions.why_it_matters: The atlas states that MMP-13 is "the enzyme that cleaves the triple helix of collagen II in the lower growth plate", and uses the persistence of the Mmp13-null phenotype into adulthood as the discriminator against the transient Mmp9-null. Both halves of that are in question. Two independently generated Mmp13-null lines, both reported in 2004, disagree on persistence: inada2004 reports growth plate abnormalities persisting into adult life, while stickens2004 reports that severity increased until about 5 weeks and COMPLETELY RESOLVED by 12 weeks. And stickens2004 made the Mmp9/Mmp13 DOUBLE null, which has severely impaired endochondral bone with diminished ECM remodelling, prolonged chondrocyte survival, delayed vascular recruitment and drastically shortened bones - the authors' conclusion being that "degradation of cartilage collagen and aggrecan is a coordinated process in which MMP13 works synergistically with MMP9". Exclusive attribution to MMP-13 does not survive a synergy result. The human situation is worse for exclusivity than the mouse: haeusler2005 finds MMP-1, -9, -10, -11 AND -13 all immunopositive in human hypertrophic chondrocytes, with MMP-14 the most prominent MMP in the human growth plate and present in all zones.
gap_contradictions.what_is_known: stickens2004 confirms collagen II and aggrecan as in vivo MMP-13 substrates, so the substrate identification is strengthened, not weakened. Both lines agree that chondrocytes differentiate normally and that their exit from the plate is delayed, so the phenotype itself replicates; only its duration is disputed. Mmp9-null gives an ~8-fold lengthened plate that remodels after 3 weeks postnatal and is rescued by wild-type bone marrow transplantation (vu1998), establishing MMP-9's cellular source as marrow-derived rather than chondrocytic. MMP13 variants cause human metaphyseal anadysplasia and a frameshift short-stature allele (lu2026).
gap_contradictions.what_is_missing: No head-to-head re-examination of the two Mmp13-null lines under one histomorphometric protocol with a stated time course to 12 weeks and beyond. No quantitative measurement of collagen II cleavage neoepitope by zone in either single or the double null. No human data assigning lower-plate collagen II cleavage to any specific MMP; the human evidence is co-localisation of at least five MMPs in the same zone.
gap_contradictions.discriminating_experiment: Phenotype Mmp13-null, Mmp9-null and Mmp9;Mmp13 double-null mice from both source lines on one background, with blinded histomorphometry of hypertrophic zone height and total plate height at 2, 5, 8, 12 and 20 weeks, plus collagen II 3/4-length neoepitope immunostaining quantified by zone. Under persistence (inada2004), Mmp13-null plate height remains elevated at 20 weeks; under resolution (stickens2004), it returns to control by 12 weeks. Under MMP-13 exclusivity, neoepitope loss in the Mmp13-null equals that in the double; under synergy, the double is significantly worse than either single. Pair with the human question by staining human physeal tissue for the same neoepitope alongside MMP-13 and MMP-14.

gap_contradictions.question: Which thyroid hormone receptor isoform carries the T3 response of the long-bone growth plate chondrocyte - and does a cartilage-restricted Thra;Thrb double deletion produce a phenotype that neither single deletion produces?
gap_contradictions.why_it_matters: This atlas already carries a logged contradiction between mouse and human on this point: rabier2006 found that ALL T3 responses were abolished in TRbeta-deficient mouse rib chondrocytes and preserved in TRalpha-deficient ones, while in humans it is dominant-negative THRA variants, not THRB variants, that cause short stature and delayed bone age - THRB resistance leaves adult stature largely normal. The paralog audit finds the resolving experiment already exists outside cartilage and points at a third answer: gthe1999 shows TRalpha1(-/-)beta(-/-) double-null mice have retarded growth and bone maturation NOT found in either single receptor-deficient mouse, and states that "deletion of TRalpha1 or TRbeta individually reveals only a small proportion of the phenotypes that arise in hypothyroidism", concluding the two isoforms cooperate with or substitute for each other. If that holds in cartilage, then neither single-null phenotype assigns the chondrocyte T3 response to an isoform, and the mouse-human contradiction may be an artefact of comparing two different compensation states rather than a real species difference. The ligand cannot help: T3 binds TRalpha1 and TRbeta1 with comparable affinity, so no pharmacological experiment can separate them.
gap_contradictions.what_is_known: robson2000 places TRalpha1, TRalpha2 AND TRbeta1 protein together in reserve and proliferating rat chondrocytes, all absent from hypertrophic cells - so both receptors occupy the same cells with no relative abundance measurement. jorge2025 documents three children with heterozygous THRA variants, short stature, low free T4 and marked response to levothyroxine plus rhGH. gthe1999 supplies the double null outside cartilage. The atlas already lists rib-versus-long-bone chondrocyte differences, germline compensation, and a genuine species difference as the candidate explanations.
gap_contradictions.what_is_missing: No cartilage-restricted Thra, Thrb or Thra;Thrb conditional deletion has been reported with a growth plate readout. No relative abundance measurement of TRalpha versus TRbeta protein in growth plate of any species. No human growth plate TR localisation at all. rabier2006's germline nulls cannot distinguish "TRbeta carries the signal" from "TRalpha compensated during development in the TRalpha-null and could not in the TRbeta-null".
gap_contradictions.discriminating_experiment: Generate Col2a1-CreERT2;Thra(fl/fl), ;Thrb(fl/fl) and ;Thra(fl/fl);Thrb(fl/fl) mice, induced postnatally to avoid developmental compensation, and measure tibial growth velocity by calcein double labelling, zonal heights and Col10a1 expression, with and without T3 challenge. Under isoform-specific signalling, one single conditional reproduces the T3-unresponsive phenotype and the other does not. Under the gthe1999 redundancy model, both singles are near-normal and only the double is unresponsive. Quantify TRalpha and TRbeta protein by zone in the same animals so the abundance question is answered alongside the functional one.
